citations.review_text: Being a huge Bethesda fan, I really wanted to like this game. It has a lot of potential but really falls short of even being entertaining. It's worth stating that I have no problems running any other games in my library, but this one is incredibly buggy and the load times are absurd. The controls are difficult to remember and its easy to end up going through an endless string of menus just to find something, and even the menus take time to load. The missions can be kind of fun, but always feel short lived. Also, there is a weird bug that causes the dialog and video to be out of sync for the first thing an NPC says in a conversation. I asked for a return but they denied it as I played it for more than two hours, which is a little bit unfair because I spent half that time waiting for the thing to load.

The audio issues I've experienced in the short play time I have made this feel like a poorly dubbed movie, the frame rate issues on medium made the game unplayable. I would not recommed this game and it would take a Cyberpunk miracle to make me want to try it again.

Completely unplayable. It stutters every few seconds and just crashes on occasion. I got this game about 2 years ago and I could play it fine then; but not now. I have no clue how Bethesda could have ruined this game, when it ran fine when I played it at first. I came back to it hoping to actually beat it since I became focused on other games then. I really hope they somehow fix this buggy mess.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that space travel and movement between locations rely heavily on menus and loading screens rather than seamless transitions.

citations.review_text:
I went into Starfield expecting a Bethesda game, and that is exactly what I got—for better and for worse.

At its best, I absolutely loved it. The faction stories, companions, cities, strange planets, political conflicts, ship collecting, exploration, and endless little side stories gave me the same feeling I get from Fallout and The Elder Scrolls. I became invested in the United Colonies, joined the Freestar Rangers, infiltrated the Crimson Fleet, worked my way through Ryujin Industries, explored House Va’ruun society, and gradually uncovered the mystery behind the Artifacts and the Unity.

Despite all the criticism surrounding the game, Starfield still felt unmistakably like Bethesda to me. It is a huge sandbox filled with interesting characters, factions, lore, moral decisions, and distractions. I enjoyed inhabiting this universe, and there were many nights when I intended to play for an hour and ended up staying for several.

I also understand why the game divided people. Space travel is heavily segmented by menus, loading screens, docking animations, elevators, and transitions. You do not freely fly from a planet’s surface into orbit in the way many people hoped. The underlying technology clearly has limits, and the game never completely delivers the seamless space-exploration fantasy its setting suggests.

That bothered me less than it bothered many other players. I knew this was still built around Bethesda’s existing engine and design structure. Once I accepted that, it felt like a traditional Bethesda RPG spread across a galaxy rather than a true space simulator—and I was fine with that.

Unfortunately, this was also one of the most technically frustrating games I have ever finished.

I encountered bugs that disrupted faction finales, companion quests, DLC missions, travel, quest markers, NPC behaviour, docking states, and follower AI. One major faction finale became impossible because a defensive battery began flying away faster than my ship cou…

This game is dumb as ♥♥♥♥.

The worst part is that it actually has a good core. The lore is interesting, the setting is cool, and I genuinely like the overall theme. But the actual gameplay constantly gets buried under ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ menus, loading screens, and fast travel.

I can tolerate the cutscenes, but this is supposed to be a space exploration game and you cannot even cruise above a planet's surface with your ship. Your ship is basically just a customizable menu that teleports you from one loading screen to another even on planet surface. Nothing makes you feel like you are actually travelling anywhere. You select a destination from a menu, watch an animation, spawn in a tiny area, walk through another procedural location, and then open the menu again.

The inventory system is probably the most annoying part. Almost nothing in the game makes logical sense, yet they suddenly care about realism when it comes to ship storage. Apparently, an enormous interstellar spaceship with a grav drive cannot hold more materials than a small garage. And the only reason for that limitation seems to be forcing players to build outposts and interact with another tedious system.

The game has a genuinely interesting universe and a solid foundation, but the developers somehow designed almost every mechanic to destroy the feeling of exploration. It does not feel like a space adventure. It feels like navigating a collection of menus with occasional shooting in between.

I love the concept behind this game, and I’ve always been a fan of Bethesda. However, there are two things that really detract from the experience and mean I can’t recommend it:
1. The game freezes and crashes: it’s very frustrating when you can’t play for even an hour straight before the game crashes for no apparent reason.
2. There are far too many loading screens. Even within the same city, there are loading screens just to move between districts. There’s no excuse for this in this day and age.

​Honestly, as someone who never really got into Skyrim, playing Starfield has finally made me see the appeal of that classic Bethesda RPG formula. There’s definitely a hook here. It’s got a massive universe, really cool lore, and mechanics like settlement building that are super addictive once you get into them. That said, it’s a bit of a mixed bag, and it definitely has some old-school quirks that hold it back from being a masterpiece.

​First off, performance-wise on PC, it’s actually solid. Running it at 1440p on High settings, I get a really smooth 90 FPS indoors, and it holds a steady 60 FPS even when you’re running around the big, built-up cities. Visually, the game looks great, but it definitely lacks depth in the lighting department, which can make some areas look a bit flat.

​The biggest issue is that a lot of the game feels like it belongs in the Xbox 360 era. The amount of unavoidable loading screens you have to sit through just to get anywhere completely kills the immersion. Luckily, the Free Lanes update came out and fixed a lot of the traversal issues, which massively helped modernize the overall feel of the game.

​If you like "cozy games," you’ll love the exploration side of it at first. Planet hopping, scanning stuff, and just wandering around is super chill and easy to get lost in. But fair warning: after you've hit a handful of planets in your first 50 hours or so, the magic kinda fades, and it loses its shine because you start seeing the same patterns. It also lacks the depth of other modern RPGs—the enemy AI is pretty brain-dead, and the stealth mechanics are incredibly basic, which sucks because the game tries to convince you that stealth is a viable way to play.

​As for the DLCs, they’re hit and miss. Terran Armada is actually a blast and has a really good story, but it’s way too short and honestly ends just as it’s getting really good. On the flip side, Shattered Space was a total letdown. It adds some neat lore for that specific clan, but …

Endless walking: its true. you walk a lot. I enjoys this style of play a lot, its very relaxing and I like reading the stats of the various species.

Gave this game a third shot and started to realize it became more fun if I treated it as an older RPG.
Sadly, the game's writing is mostly lacking in several areas. With that said, the atmosphere is as always amazing as it is with most Bethesda games. Trying to find anything similar in other studios RPG's keeps me looking back at the Bethesda games. 

Thankfully, the game gives the opportunity of almost rewriting your character with the in-game surgery centers and thus I remade my character as a pirate, hoping to avoid talking and story expositions and focus more on action and exploration and that was some of the most fun I've had in an RPG in a while. 
The missions was extremely fun and gave some (I think) missions unique loot which I always love. When I finished the story I realized that it payed enough for me to build a new ship which was a great trophy in it self. 

Lastly, I want to really express how happy I am in that there is finally a game where I can build my own spaceship and actually just be able to walk around in it, and it not looking like ass. There are a lot of areas I wish could be improved upon in the ship building, but I'm enjoying it still.

Edit: This game has so much to offer, there is probably something that might be enjoyable. If you don't enjoy an aspect of the game, I recommend avoiding it.

Starfield has some nice moments, but those moments are way too short for me. Questlines are a bit too short, even when they have solid foundations. Exploration doesn't feel meaningful. In the end, when you explore a hundred planets and survey them, that doesn't leave you with a solid understanding of flora and fauna, you just got XP and some money.

All in all, the game is too shallow for me. It tries a whole lot of things and does them ok-ish, but I never really get drawn into it. There is no real flow to it all, it just feels like I am checking off a todo list.

Some moments, when you are on a planet and see the surrounding solar system, there are glimpses of atmosphere, but they are at odds with the generic locations and soulless content. It doesn't feel like I am experiencing something, but rather than I am playing. And I just prefer more immersion.

That said, it’s a bit of a mixed bag, and it definitely has some old-school quirks that hold it back from being a masterpiece.

​First off, performance-wise on PC, it’s actually solid. Running it at 1440p on High settings, I get a really smooth 90 FPS indoors, and it holds a steady 60 FPS even when you’re running around the big, built-up cities. Visually, the game looks great, but it definitely lacks depth in the lighting department, which can make some areas look a bit flat.

​The biggest issue is that a lot of the game feels like it belongs in the Xbox 360 era. The amount of unavoidable loading screens you have to sit through just to get anywhere completely kills the immersion. Luckily, the Free Lanes update came out and fixed a lot of the traversal issues, which massively helped modernize the overall feel of the game.

​If you like "cozy games," you’ll love the exploration side of it at first. Planet hopping, scanning stuff, and just wandering around is super chill and easy to get lost in. But fair warning: after you've hit a handful of planets in your first 50 hours or so, the magic kinda fades, and it loses its shine because you start seeing the same patterns. It also lacks the depth of other modern RPGs—the enemy AI is pretty brain-dead, and the stealth mechanics are incredibly basic, which sucks because the game tries to convince you that stealth is a viable way to play.

​As for the DLCs, they’re hit and miss. Terran Armada is actually a blast and has a really good story, but it’s way too short and honestly ends just as it’s getting really good. On the flip side, Shattered Space was a total letdown. It adds some neat lore for that specific clan, but …

You can explore a vast galaxy and find the same can of pop on the same table in the same building on every world. The only cool biomes are just small areas to scan and shoud of been the whole planets. Im So Bored!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game freezes and crashes during play.

citations.review_text: Honestly cant recommend the game, for how long it was in development and been released its almost criminal on how many times it will crash.

I love the concept behind this game, and I’ve always been a fan of Bethesda. However, there are two things that really detract from the experience and mean I can’t recommend it:
1. The game freezes and crashes: it’s very frustrating when you can’t play for even an hour straight before the game crashes for no apparent reason.
2. There are far too many loading screens. Even within the same city, there are loading screens just to move between districts. There’s no excuse for this in this day and age.

cohorts.summary: Veterans find enjoyment in ship building and faction quests despite ongoing progression bugs, repetitive exploration, and unengaging main quests.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the main questline is boring and unengaging.

citations.review_text: The barebones of this game is great it's just a shame it suffers from Bethesda's writing and bugs. I think the early game is actually more compelling and interesting than the later game where the main quest drops the ball super hard and becomes an incredibly boring excuse to shove you into NG+ as it felt like they pivoted from their original idea super hard into what the main quest ended up being. Another case of "good idea, not great execution" from Bethesda but fun enough to recommend playing playing and buying. But maybe when it's on deep discount.

There are a few things Starfield does well. The ship-building system is genuinely fun, and designing, upgrading, and customizing ships was easily the highlight of my experience. If you enjoy tinkering with builds and creating your own spacecraft, there's a lot to like.

Unfortunately, that's where most of my praise ends.

The finished game feels nothing like what was marketed before release. The main quest is painfully boring—so much so that it almost feels intentional. I kept waiting for it to get interesting, but it never really did. The side quests aren't much better, with very few standing out as memorable.

Exploration is also a huge disappointment. The planets are mostly barren, and after a while you start seeing the same handful of points of interest repeated over and over. Instead of feeling like you're exploring a massive galaxy, it quickly becomes repetitive and lifeless.

For the price, I can't recommend it. If there were ever a AAA game that felt like the product of laziness and chasing profits over delivering a compelling experience, this would be near the top of the list.

My recommendation? Wait until it's heavily discounted. Maybe by 2036, if you can find it for around $3, it'll be worth checking out.

Alright, I gotta be 100% honest when writing this review.

The game isn't totally terrible..

It's got some serious issues, yes. Mainly the fact that the main story is the least interesting thing to ever exist and has no incentivization to actually complete at all. I still haven't completed the main story, not even once. That's how boring it's quests are and how little it incentivizes me to play it. 

Some other issues I have are as follows:

Ship customization; Ships are too big for my liking, I love small fighter type ships, and I love flying solo with no companions. Why am I not allowed to build a tiny little ship that's just a fighter? Why does everything have to be five times the size of a double decker bus?

The SysDef vs Crimson Fleet storyline; This is by far the second most boring storyline in the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. I am a tried and true law obedient, if I ever disobey the law it will probably be the same day I die. So imagine my disappointment when I find out to take out the crimson fleet, I have to do some super sleuth, 007, hitman action. I HATE these kinds of missions. Especially because SysDef CLEARLY has the resources and intel to take out the Crimson Fleet well before this, the story is USELESS. I'd rather spend my time and effort shooting every crimson fleet ship in the universe than spend another MINUTE amongst those ANIMALS the game calls Pirates. Worst decision ever, absolute garbage, I HATE the Crimson Fleet, I HATE IT.

Upgrading gear; It's just bad, I don't understand why you can't just enhance the gun normally, without it just getting higher damage number. I feel like legendary guns with special perks should get enhancing tiers, to incentivize a hunt for that kind of gear, and then you can improve the power/duration of the special perks by enhancing the tier of the weapon/armor.

The good stuff, stuff I like:

The UC Vanguard Anti-Xeno questline was fun, I enjoyed it, it was well written, and it was genuinely fun to play thr…

I had high hopes for Starfield. There are so many space games and mediocre RPGs, but a true Bethesda experience would be awesome. Instead it's a weak ripoff of No Man's Sky with better visuals and great starships, but far worse space combat and flight and honestly the most lame and dull main quest anyone could come up with. It makes the NMS overall story seem epic, which isn't saying much. What a wasted opportunity, and the total lack of ownership of Creations compatibility when Creations are the only thing that make it worth playing, and the resultant constant CTD's with Creations making it unplayable, it's a disaster. If they spend the same effort Cyberpunk, NMS and other games do to constantly improve it, maybe someday it'll be worthwhile, but it's terrible today.

Pretty far into the main campaign and at most I find it to be just alright.  Now I haven't finished the main line yet so I could have a different opinion afterwards.   I'm 146 hours in at the moment and it has been said already multiple times but the real star here is the side quests, especially the faction based ones in my opinion.  So far each side story for the factions are engaging and different from one another and keeps everything interesting.  

The gunplay is solid.  I can't comment on outposts since I've only ever put down a beacon in my playthrough so far and quickly wanted to get back into the story.  

Exploration can be hit or miss.  Sometimes I feel like its a chore to run around a section of a planet just to discover something that is almost identical to others I've found.  However, there are some things that can be found and pull you back in.   Then I'll find myself spending hours running around a section just to identify everything.  Get the vehicle, which makes this process faster but sometimes I prefer running.  Controls of the vehicle can remind you of the Mako.

Speaking of the Mako, which I'm sure has been said before,  I feel Starfield is a mix of Fallout, No Man's Sky and Mass Effect.  Now I may be biased since the ME series is probably my favorite video game series and I'm also a massive Fallout fan with thousands of hours into both.  No Man's Sky I also enjoyed but put it down after maybe 50 or so hours and never returned, but plan to at some point. 

Now Bethesda and their bugs and "charm".  Surprisingly, I haven't run into many bugs, or any of note that really messed up my gameplay.  I can say that the game does have its crash moments randomly.  Most of the time it is when I load the game and the title screen is playing.  Could be an issue with my system so who knows.  While in game, it has maybe happened 5 or 6 times which is pretty good for over 140 hours.

I really wanted a space Skyrim from Bethesda—spaceships instead of dragons, quests, a great story, and all the little details that make Bethesda games special.

I tried to play Starfield twice, but both times I ended up with the same result: it's just boring. When you see the same facility for the third time on the third planet, with the boss hiding in the exact same spot, you'll just uninstall it too.

C'mon, Todd!

This game is a very generated empty tech-monster and does not even look as good as it should. As an old Bethesda enjoyer I do not care about loading screens. Or bad face animation. Or boring main quests.
But Todd, if you can not make an interesting game anymore.. what's wrong with Bethesda these days? Everybody enjoyed handcrafted, nice explorable, great sidequest line filled RPGs where you can sandbox the sheet out of your characters. This game is so simplified and polished, unendgy and generic - it is completely not worth it if you are used to classic Bethesda RPGs. 
So - if you liked Oblivion and Morrowind (yeah I think they were better than Skyriim) then Starfield is probably not for you. 
Graphics are enjoyable and the best thing about that is the ship builder. But hey - NMS has more generated worlds and added a ship building tool last year - do not waste your time with starfield.

I am really enjoying the game. The ship building and combat are both a lot of fun.

[h1]Better Than Launch, But Still Falls Short[/h1]

Starfield is a much better game in 2026 than it was at launch. The patches have improved the experience, and I had a good time overall.

That said, Shattered Space was disappointing. I eventually left the DLC and went back to exploring the galaxy because I was having more fun doing random things than playing the expansion.

The NG+ system is an interesting idea, but it never feels fully realized. There is also a lot of repetition, and the game still doesn't have the depth of mod support that Skyrim had at a similar point in its life.

On the positive side, ship building is very fun. I also enjoyed base building far more than I expected.

One confession: I always make sure my ships have enough toilets so none of the crew has to wait. If that makes me weird... so be it.

Starfield is one of those games that is almost great. It has flashes of brilliance mixed with repetitive systems and unrealized ideas. Despite its flaws, I enjoyed my time with it.

7/10. Worth playing, especially if you can pick it up on sale.

Firstly..  I don't understand why SF gets so much hate.. but I came from NMS and FO is a long term main of mine and the blend of the two.. well I loved it. Couple of bugs... and if you used terminal a previous save didn't wipe the temrinal.. and so I lost all my achivements.. aside from that.. what's not to like?

Customization of cool ships? check! .. main story.. yes there were many many stories but like most FO and ES games.. you don't really need to care about the main story.. they are there for once you thrown MANY hours in to a game. citations.review_text:
I have put over 200 hours into this game and while it may not seem like much in the large scale i have loved every bit of this game, there are a few mission bugs still present like "Talk with Sarah" and "location of ECS Constellation" but i have found that with those the developers have been working tirelessly to fix and improve this game. 

I took a break before the April Update and picked it back up after the July Update and absolutely love the features they have added. While i haven't tried all of them or even ran into some of the new adds, the features i have used such as the Cruise feature is very handy when traveling because it lets you upgrade armor, weapons, or even do research while moving to your new objective. or the new Resource Information and Research screen in the Hud menu, i love how i can get rid of items that i had tracked for old weapons or upgrades that i don't even have anymore. I like how you can even see where the items are and individually track or remove items to make it easier.

I cant wait to keep playing and see what else had been added after looking at the recent Update post and I thank the developers for continuing to make this game enjoyable and relaxing to play or intense to play based on how you feel your story wants to go.

Long story short. I tried to like the game. Have been a fan of Bethesda Games for a while now. Since Morrowind. And I've had my worries from one game to the next, but ultimately I enjoyed each and every Elder Scrolls and Fallout game I have played. Starfield has shown that the things that worried me won out at Bethesda. I tried. I really tried. I looked through a bunch of nooks and crannies to try to find something I would enjoy. I found a few fun quests, but not enough for me to recommend this game.

On top of all of that. It is buggy and breaks too much. Like currently, was going to give Terran Armada a try, but it broke in the FIRST QUESTLINE! The hatch I need to drop down to go through the ship that was attacked doesn't actually open when I activate it. I looked it up and it is what I am supposed to do. Looks like it's just broken. I did some trouble-shooting, but I keep asking myself why I am trying so hard to find something enjoyable about this game.

I will say that the game feels like it had certain care paid to parts of it, but not others. And it definitely seems like more care and attention was paid to the United Colonies than the Freestar Collective, especially in the faction questlines. With seeming a bit more negative portrayal of the FC in the Colony Wars, and that the UC was more in the right. And the worst part? You can hear people complaining about the Colony Wars, about any source of tension in the gameworld, and it always just hits flat. Side with the Crimson Fleet? Don't worry, nobody cares. Side with the cops? Still no one seems to really care. Join the UC Vanguard? Kind of fun, but still doesn't seem like it matters much. Freestar Ranger? Who cares? Ryujin operative with basically a super power? Can use it a bit, but still really lackluster. Feel like something along the lines of Skyrim civil war sort of decisions and questlines, or like choosing a faction over others in Fallout 4 would have made the game hit hard. Instead of a bland, static ga…

I gave this game multiple chances.

3 different playthroughs, all at different stages in the game's lifecycle. One at launch, one later on, and then a recent, heavily modded version. 

And all 3 times, the bugs were the reason I had to stop. Quests wouldn't trigger right, some questlines would come to a dead-stop because they'd bug out and wouldn't continue, I'd try waiting, try jumping around in my ship, restarting the game, everything. 

The game has some cool elements, but some cool elements doesn't make it worth playing. 

The game needed to be in the oven for a few more years, it's undercooked.

Almost 3 years later & it is still buggy as hell. The concept is cool. The execution is lack-luster. It's kind of sad when indie games are more stable than this. The game is pretty good but, prepare for all sorts of headaches.
